rationale: CATCH-CLAUSE RECEIVER TYPING. `on MyErr catch (e)` writes the exception's type in the clause; the analyzer collected the BINDING but not the TYPE, so `e.mark()` published a bare `calls -> mark` with `receiverCause: receiverTypeUnknown` while `mark` is declared in the same file three lines up. The fix records the `on` type for every name in the clause's `catch_parameters` child (both names of `catch (e, st)`: Dart's rule is that the second parameter is the stack trace of the SAME exception), with the receiver contract's `annotation` evidence class — the source WROTE the type, so this is evidence, not inference. The untyped catch is the boundary: `catch (e)` names no type, the cut must remain, and no owner may be fabricated (a wrong owner is worse than none — the store WITHDRAWS the name binding on an owner-carrying row).

expectRelationships.note: THE FIX — the caught exception's type is the `on` clause's, so the call target is spelled and the owner channel carries the type. Before the fix this row was `calls -> mark` with `receiverCause: receiverTypeUnknown`.
the READ arm on a caught exception (`e.code`) — both arms must see the type, or the fix only moves calls.

THE TWO-NAME FORM — `catch (e, st)` types both names with the same exception type. A fix that only typed `catch_parameters`'s FIRST identifier passes the single-name case and fails no row there; this case is what makes the loop over names load-bearing.
BOUNDARY, positive side: an UNTYPED catch still binds `e`, and its reads publish the family binding spelling. The absence of a type must not remove the binding.

forbidRelationships.note: THE PRE-FIX SHAPE — the bare leaf must be gone once the written type is collected. Forbidding the exact old row is what makes this fixture able to fail.
the same pre-fix shape on the read arm.
THE ALIAS IS NOT THE OWNER — `MyErr` is the class-like name the store looks up; `e` is the value's name.
NO INFERENCE FOR AN UNTYPED CATCH — `catch (e)` names no type anywhere at the site; an owner here would be the guessed type the contract forbids.
a caught exception read is a BINDING read (family spelling), never a bare declaration read.
